acceptanceCriteria: Given a complete valid control fixture, parseControl returns the record and validateControl returns [] with zero errors.
ControlRecord requires schemaVersion 'rorca.ssdlc-control-record.v1'; an unknown schemaVersion is rejected.
Given a control object with controlId omitted, validateControl returns at least one error whose path includes controlId.
Given a control object with sourceStrength 'unverified', validateControl returns an error whose path includes sourceStrength.
Given a control object whose sourceReferences contains an item lacking genesisEvidenceId, validateControl returns an error whose path includes sourceReferences and the offending index.
Given a control object with version '1.0', validateControl returns an error whose path includes version, because '1.0' is not strict semver.

Every requiredEvidence entry validates classification, allowed source types, required subject or release bindings, minimum trust, evidence depth, and freshness; an untyped string requirement is rejected.
Given the JSON Schema artifact at control-schema.json, a record rejected by validateControl is also rejected by ajv JSON Schema validation.

PHASES exports exactly ['intake','requirements','architecture','implementation','validation','security','staging','qa','merge','production','learn'] in that order and MISSION_STAGE_BY_PHASE maps them to intent, plan, build, verify, release, or learn.
A consumer fixture from the assurance compiler validates through this schema without a second control-catalog type.
userStories.description: Implement the canonical ControlRecord contract as the sole source of truth for SSDLC controls. Create backend/src/ssdlc/schema/control-schema.ts exporting PHASES, MISSION_STAGE_BY_PHASE, SOURCE_STRENGTHS, FAILURE_SEVERITIES, EVIDENCE_DEPTHS, ControlRecord, EvidenceRequirement, parseControl(unknown), and validateControl(unknown): ValidationError[]. Emit backend/src/ssdlc/schema/control-schema.json as a JSON Schema draft 2020-12 artifact. ControlRecord has schemaVersion 'rorca.ssdlc-control-record.v1', strict semver version, controlId, phase, objective, applicability, source references, structured requiredEvidence, failure severity, exception policy, and skillRefs. Each EvidenceRequirement specifies classification, allowedSourceTypes, required subject/release bindings, minimum trust level, evidence depth, and freshness. This schema and controls.json are canonical: AAV consumes controlId and this artifact; it must not define a second catalog or controlRef shape. Follow docs/contracts/ssdlc-interoperability.md.
userStories.title: Control Catalog Schema and Validation

acceptanceCriteria: Given a Genesis bridge projection for valid evidence GEN-001, getEvidence('GEN-001') returns that exact projection and its bridge provenance.
No local function can promote pending or unreviewed evidence to approved or trusted; review state comes only from the Genesis bridge.
Given a control whose sourceReferences cites genesisEvidenceId 'GEN-999' that is not registered by Genesis, validateControlAgainstGenesis returns an error identifying 'GEN-999'.
Given a control whose sourceReferences includes a citation without a resolvable genesisEvidenceId, validateControlAgainstGenesis rejects the record.
Given two projected evidence records sharing contradictionGroup 'authz-conflict', detectContradictions returns exactly one conflict object containing both genesisEvidenceIds and the group name.
Given GEN-002 projected as superseding GEN-001, resolveAuthority('GEN-001') returns GEN-002 and marks GEN-001 superseded.
The source-authority suite covers projection, reject, supersession, contradiction, and attempted local-promotion denial paths.
userStories.description: Implement the Genesis source authority projection at backend/src/ssdlc/genesis/source-authority.ts. Genesis is the sole authority for evidence review status and access. Define a validated local EvidenceRecord projection { genesisEvidenceId, sourceTitle, exactCitation, evidenceStrength, supersedes?: string[], supersededBy?: string, contradictionGroup?: string } sourced from the existing Genesis bridge; it must never independently approve, trust, or promote evidence. Export getEvidence, resolveAuthority, detectContradictions, validateControlAgainstGenesis, and test-fixture registration only. Integrate with US-001 so every source reference resolves to a Genesis evidence id; raw-prose-only references are rejected. Contradictions and supersession remain explicit and carry Genesis provenance. HMG-003 consumes this same bridge-compatible projection.
userStories.title: Genesis Source Authority Projection

acceptanceCriteria: Given a profile { productProfile: 'api-service', riskProfile: [], domainRegulatory: [] }, the resolver includes every control with applicability.universal true and every control whose productProfiles includes 'api-service', and excludes controls whose productProfiles is ['cli'].
Given a profile with riskProfile containing 'safety-critical', every active control with applicability.riskProfiles including 'safety-critical' receives evidenceDepth 'independent-verification'.
Given a profile with domainRegulatory ['finance'], controls with applicability.domainRegulatory including 'finance' are active and controls tagged only ['healthcare'] are excluded.
Given an L5 specTaskOverride { controlId: 'CTRL-X', action: 'exclude', requirementId: 'REQ-42' }, the resolver excludes CTRL-X and the resolutionLog records REQ-42 as the override source.
Given an empty profile { productProfile: null, riskProfile: [], domainRegulatory: [], workspaceConventions: [], specTaskOverrides: [] }, the resolver returns all L0 universal controls.
Calling resolveActiveControls twice with identical profiles returns deep-equal activeControlIds and evidenceDepthByControlId.
The jest suite resolver.test.ts covers L0-L5 selection, depth derivation, and override paths and passes.
userStories.description: Implement the layered applicability resolver at backend/src/ssdlc/applicability/resolver.ts. Profile shape: { productProfile: 'cli'|'library'|'web-frontend'|'api-service'|'mobile'|'data-pipeline'|'ai-ml'|'infrastructure'|null, riskProfile: string[], domainRegulatory: string[], workspaceConventions?: string[], specTaskOverrides?: Array<{ controlId, action: 'include'|'exclude', evidenceDepthOverride?, requirementId }> }. L0 controls with applicability.universal true are always active. L1 product profile selects by applicability.productProfiles. L2 risk profile selects by applicability.riskProfiles. L3 domain-regulatory overlay selects by applicability.domainRegulatory. L4 workspace conventions and L5 spec-task requirements apply as overrides on top of L0-L3. Export resolveActiveControls(profile) returning { activeControlIds, evidenceDepthByControlId, resolutionLog }. Evidence depth derivation: controls tied to safety-critical, aviation, or privacy-regulated receive independent-verification; controls tied to data-modifying, financial-side-effects, external-integration, or privileged-admin receive artifact; remaining active controls receive self-attestation; L4/L5 overrides are applied last and recorded in resolutionLog. Add jest tests in backend/src/ssdlc/applicability/resolver.test.ts.
userStories.title: Layered Applicability Resolver L0-L5

acceptanceCriteria: Given fixture controls covering all 11 phases with at least one control per mandatory family, compileGates returns exactly 11 ordered phase control groups from intake through learn.
Each phase group contains phase, controlIds, families, and structured evidence requirements; every controlId appears in at least one family array.
The readiness projection contains exactly six stages in order: intent, plan, build, verify, release, learn.
The phase mapping is intake->intent; requirements and architecture->plan; implementation->build; validation and security->verify; staging, qa, merge, and production->release; learn->learn.
Learn is explicitly non-blocking, while unresolved applicable controls block only their projected non-learn stage.

Gate families match the brief, including intake need-validity/scope-boundaries/risk-classification, requirements completeness/verifiability/traceability/quality-attributes, security threat-control-verification/authz-boundaries/secrets/supply-chain/vulnerability-response, and learn incident-analysis/prediction-vs-outcome/delivery-metrics/control-effectiveness/improvement-candidates.
Given a fixture set with no control mapping to qa family independent-evidence-review, compileGates reports the missing family for qa.
Each evidence requirement derives from US-001 and contains the evidence depth computed by US-003.
The gate-compiler suite covers phase order, six-stage projection, family coverage, learn non-blocking behavior, and missing-family reporting.
userStories.description: Implement the phase compiler at backend/src/ssdlc/gates/gate-compiler.ts. FAMILY_MAP defines mandatory control families for each of the 11 canonical phases. Compile active controls from US-003 into 11 phase control groups with evidence requirements, then project them into the six Mission stages: intent=intake; plan=requirements+architecture; build=implementation; verify=validation+security; release=staging+qa+merge+production; learn=learn. The first five stages may block delivery when applicable controls are unresolved; learn is asynchronous and non-blocking. Risk, regulation, or governed exception may expose an approval inside its stage. This compiler owns mandatory-control selection; AAV-005 only binds mechanisms and criteria to its output.
userStories.title: Phase Control Groups and Stage Readiness Compiler

acceptanceCriteria: Given a stage whose active controls each have matching current canonical lifecycle evidence, evaluateGate returns pass and every control result includes authority support, demonstrated evidence, and evaluated skill.
Given an active control with no matching canonical lifecycle evidence, evaluateGate returns blocked with a reason naming the missing evidence requirement.
Evidence with stale, mismatched, or absent spec hash, commit SHA, required release identity, trust level, depth, or freshness is rejected for the control.
Given a control with allowedNotApplicable true and evidence-backed not-applicable evidence, evaluateGate records not-applicable and does not block the stage.
Given a control with allowedNotApplicable false and no submitted evidence, evaluateGate remains blocked.
Given a control with an expired or disallowed exception, evaluateGate remains blocked and names the exception authority or expiry.
Given a resolver-assigned independent-verification requirement and evidence without independent verification, evaluateGate returns blocked.
Learn outcomes are evaluated for traceability but do not block a completed release.
The gate-evaluator suite covers canonical-envelope matching, identity mismatch, pass, missing evidence, not-applicable, exception, depth, freshness, and learn non-blocking paths.
userStories.description: Implement the mandatory gate evaluation engine at backend/src/ssdlc/evaluation/gate-evaluator.ts. evaluateGate consumes only canonical rorca.lifecycle-evidence.v1 records (or validated hermes.evidence.v1 ingress normalized into that record) against US-001 structured EvidenceRequirements and returns a GateEvaluationTrace. It aggregates phase results into the US-004 stage projection. A control with no matching current evidence, no evidence-backed not-applicable determination, and no valid exception is blocked. Evidence must bind the exact spec hash and release identity required by the control and be newer than the subject mutation. AAV kernel outcomes are internal and must be normalized by AAV-006 before reaching this evaluator.
userStories.title: Canonical Lifecycle Evidence and Exception Evaluation

acceptanceCriteria: Given bindSkill called with a SkillRecord whose controlIds includes an existing catalog controlId, the registry stores the skill and resolveSkillRefs returns its current version.
Given a control whose skillRefs includes an unresolved skill, resolveSkillRefs returns an error naming it.

Given an AAV phase-review StructuredFinding with blocker status for an active control, the matching stage becomes blocked and the stored finding retains identity, control, skill, story, status, and evidence references.
Given findings with pass status only, the gate verdict remains pass.
Given a skill upgrade from v1 to v2, the control record's skillRefs remains stable and resolution returns v2 with an upgrade note.
A finding missing controlId or skillId is rejected, and an alternate phase-review finding shape is rejected.
The skill-binding suite covers binding, unresolved refs, AAV finding ingestion, blocker gating, upgrade stability, and validation.
userStories.description: Implement skill binding at backend/src/ssdlc/skills/skill-registry.ts and findings ingestion at backend/src/ssdlc/skills/findings.ts. SkillRecord { skillId, name, version, controlIds[], implementationRef } binds only existing US-001 controlIds. StructuredFinding is the sole finding shape for AAV-012 through AAV-018: { findingId, controlId, skillId, requirementId?, storyId?, status: 'pass'|'fail'|'blocker', evidenceRefs, message }. ingestFindings validates each finding and blocks the matching US-004 stage when a blocker maps to an active control. No phase-review agent may introduce an alternate finding store or shape.
userStories.title: Skill Binding and Structured Findings

acceptanceCriteria: Given a production outcome where a defect reached production despite passing validation tests, consumeProductionOutcome returns a pending-review test-class-failed-to-predict-defect candidate.
Given a production outcome recording rework caused by a granted exception, it returns an exception-caused-rework candidate.
Given a control that produced no signal across all evaluated gates for a release, it returns a control-produced-no-signal candidate at the configured threshold.
Given a model performance record with task-class underperformance, it returns a model-underperformed-on-task-class candidate.
Given two identical outcomes, the second increments signalCount on the existing candidate and creates no new candidateId.
AAV heal and run outcomes enter only through consumeProductionOutcome and return this canonical candidate shape.
Given a pending-review candidate, applyCandidate without approved review errors and leaves controls.json byte-for-byte unchanged.
The learn-loop suite covers all four types, deduplication, AAV adapter input, pending-review-only behavior, and the no-silent-rewrite invariant.
userStories.description: Implement the only learn-loop candidate store at backend/src/ssdlc/learn/learn-loop.ts. consumeProductionOutcome(outcome) classifies a production or healing outcome into reviewable Genesis candidates of four types: test-class-failed-to-predict-defect, exception-caused-rework, control-produced-no-signal, and model-underperformed-on-task-class. Candidate shape is { candidateId, type, controlId, phase, evidenceRef, signalCount, status: 'pending-review'|'approved'|'rejected' }. Deduplicate by (type, controlId, evidenceRefHash). AAV-022 adapts its outcomes into this function; it must not implement a second candidate shape or store. applyCandidate requires approved status and explicit authorized actor; no candidate auto-approves or silently rewrites the catalog.
userStories.title: Canonical Learn-Loop Candidate Generation

acceptanceCriteria: controls.json contains between 20 and 40 ControlRecord records and every record passes US-001 validation.
Every phase in PHASES has at least one control and US-004 reports no missing mandatory family.
Every source reference resolves to a Genesis evidence id in genesis-evidence.json; no source reference is raw prose without an evidence id.
Every control's source strength, failure severity, exception policy, skill refs, schema version, and structured evidence requirements match US-001.
Every evidence requirement has a declared real adapter or an explicit governed human or approval route; no required evidence is an unimplementable string.
The catalog contains at least one cited control for ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010, ISO/IEC 25010, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119, NIST SP 800-218, and DORA with exact clause or section citations.
The catalog suite validates every criterion and includes an AAV consumer fixture resolving controls by controlId.
userStories.description: Curate and ship the initial canonical catalog at backend/src/ssdlc/catalog/controls.json and the Genesis evidence projection fixture at backend/src/ssdlc/catalog/genesis-evidence.json. Include 20 to 40 US-001-valid controls across all 11 phase categories so US-004 reports no missing mandatory family. Source controls from ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022, ISO/IEC 25010:2023, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119, NIST SP 800-218 SSDF, and DORA delivery research with exact citations. Every control provides structured evidence requirements and every requirement resolves either to a real AAV-019 adapter or an explicit governed human or approval route. This is the only catalog consumed by AAV.

acceptanceCriteria: All seven schemas exist in shared/contracts/source.ts and the backend mirror with exact version strings and closed enum parity
Every SourceRef carries a sha256 contentHash and a valid reviewStatus/sensitivity/authority from closed enums
IntentDispositionV1 accepts only the six dispositions; unknown disposition is rejected at parse
Bundle hash is derived deterministically from userIntent + included sources + selected sections + citations
Automated tests include fixtures that accept a valid source bundle and reject each invalid case: unknown enum, external or traversing locator, missing content hash, and mismatched bundle hash.
Frontend and backend typechecks pass; no changes to existing mission.ts contracts
userStories.description: Add SourceRefV1, SourceBundleV1, SourceCitationV1, SourceConflictV1, ContextCompilationReceiptV1, IntentEnvelopeV1, and IntentDispositionV1 to shared/contracts/source.ts (and the rootDir-safe backend mirror backend/src/lib/source-contracts.ts) following the existing mission.ts versioning pattern (schemaVersion per contract, strict Zod, closed enums with explicit unknown). SourceRefV1 carries kind (genesis_package | genesis_evidence | local_file | url | github_issue | github_pr | linear_document | rorca_mission | inline), locator, title, contentHash sha256, sourceVersion, reviewStatus (approved | trusted | pending | unreviewed | external), sensitivity, authority (user_mandated | approved_context | supporting_evidence), and selectedSections. SourceBundleV1 records bundleId, bundleHash, userIntent, workspaceRef (EntityRefV1), includedSources, excludedSources with reasons, conflicts, assumptions, truncations, citations, compiledAt. IntentDispositionV1 is a closed union: answer | clarification_required | mission_draft | existing_mission_action | memory_candidate | denied, each with targetRef, draftHash, rationale, requiredDecision, permittedAction. Reject external/nested locators, unhashed content, overloaded statuses, and client-authored arbitrary actions.

acceptanceCriteria: SourceAdapter interface and registry compile with strict types and are exported from the backend lib index
Registry returns an honest unavailable result for unknown locator schemes instead of throwing or guessing
Fetching a source yields a VersionedSource with content hash, revision, and selected section bounds
No command execution or URL opening occurs anywhere in resolve/fetch/normalize
Focused unit tests cover known adapter, unknown scheme, missing authority, and oversized content truncation
Backend typecheck passes
userStories.description: Define the SourceAdapter interface (canResolve, resolve, fetch, normalize) and a registry in backend/src/lib/source-adapters.ts. Each adapter returns typed SourceCandidate[] from resolve and a frozen VersionedSource from fetch (content + exact revision + sha256 hash + byte/section bounds). Adapters must fail closed on unresolvable locators, unsupported schemes, missing authority, or redaction-required content. The registry exposes listAdapters(), resolveFor(locator), and a bounded normalize pipeline that never executes commands and treats source content strictly as data.
userStories.title: Source adapter framework with registry and honest failure states

acceptanceCriteria: Resolving an approved Genesis package returns SourceRefV1 with bridge-derived reviewStatus approved and complete sha256 hashes.
Pending or unreviewed candidates resolve with bridge-derived pending/unreviewed state, never approved.
Restricted evidence is redacted in the compiled bundle with a visible marker and never included as raw text.
The adapter emits GenesisProvenanceSchema-compatible metadata and the same provenance fields consumed by US-002.
No adapter path can grant approval, trust, or a sensitivity exception locally.
Focused tests cover approved, pending, missing-package, restricted-sensitivity, and attempted-local-promotion paths; backend typecheck passes.
userStories.description: Implement the Genesis adapter (kind genesis_package | genesis_evidence) in backend/src/lib/source-adapters/genesis.ts. It resolves approved Genesis packages/evidence by id through the existing Genesis bridge/provenance surface, maps to the existing GenesisProvenanceSchema shape, and preserves bridge-derived reviewStatus approved/trusted/pending/unreviewed. Pending candidates are never presented as approved. Restricted material obeys the requesting principal's sensitivity authority and remains redacted. Selected sections reference exact evidence chunk ids and citations. Consume the US-002 Genesis authority projection; do not create a local approval registry or mutate Genesis review state.
userStories.title: Genesis source adapter resolving canonical approved provenance

acceptanceCriteria: A workspace-relative Markdown path resolves to a hashed SourceRefV1 with heading section citations
Path traversal, absolute paths outside the workspace, and missing files fail closed with ValidationError
Sections are bounded by size; oversized content truncates with an explicit truncation record, never silently
Using a file for a Mission does not write memory candidates or Genesis entries on its own
Focused tests cover heading extraction, traversal rejection, truncation, and binary/non-text rejection
Backend typecheck passes
userStories.description: Implement the local-file adapter (kind local_file) resolving paths relative to the active workspace root. It resolves the exact path (rejecting traversal), reads and normalizes Markdown/text, computes sha256, extracts heading-level sections with line ranges, and produces SourceRefV1 with selectedSections and citations to exact headings. A document used for one Mission is classified user-supplied source evidence; it is not automatically promoted to organizational knowledge. Offer capture-to-Genesis as an explicit separate action, never implicit.
userStories.title: Local file source adapter for workspace Markdown and text documents

acceptanceCriteria: Compiling two non-conflicting sources produces one SourceBundleV1 with both SourceRefs and citations
A material conflict (e.g. privacy policy vs feature PRD) produces a visible SourceConflictV1 and a clarification disposition
Source text containing instruction-like content is never executed and is visibly quoted as source data
Secrets (API keys, tokens) are redacted from the compiled bundle
Compilation is bounded: an explicit budget caps total included tokens with truncation records
Focused tests cover merge, conflict, prompt-injection, redaction, and budget paths; backend typecheck passes
userStories.description: Implement compileSourceBundle in backend/src/lib/source-compiler.ts. It merges user-mandated sources (user_mandated), approved organizational context (Direction Stack, approved Genesis knowledge, conventions), and supporting evidence (code, git, prior Missions) into a SourceBundleV1. It detects material conflicts across sources and against higher-authority direction, emitting SourceConflictV1 entries and requiring user resolution only when scope, safety, or acceptance is affected. It separates source content from instructions: external content is data, never executable instructions; secrets are redacted; and a bounded extraction contract prevents token blowup. It reuses buildForgeContextBundle for the Rorca-native context side.
userStories.title: Context compiler with conflict detection and prompt-injection separation

acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/hermes/intent returns strict IntentDispositionV1 with rationale for all six dispositions.
A request referencing an existing mission id routes to existing_mission_action with the exact EntityRef.
A request with explicit source refs and no mission routes to mission_draft and includes the compiled bundle hash.
Replaying the same idempotencyKey returns the same disposition without duplicate side effects.
Requests referencing another workspace's mission are denied.
Every disposition records declared audit identity and authority mode; accidental admin fallback is rejected.
Focused route tests cover all dispositions, idempotency, workspace isolation, and authority; Swagger annotations and backend typecheck pass.
userStories.description: Add POST /api/hermes/intent accepting IntentEnvelopeV1 and returning IntentDispositionV1. Classification is deterministic-first: explicit source refs and existing-mission refs drive mission_draft / existing_mission_action; read-only question phrasing yields answer; memory-candidate phrasing yields memory_candidate; ambiguous scope yields clarification_required; policy violation yields denied. Model synthesis may assist only after deterministic signals. The endpoint is idempotent by workspace-scoped idempotencyKey and uses the AAV-023 declared service-audit/operator-dispatch authority model. A mission_draft continues only through HMG-007's source bundle -> persist -> controls -> assurance compilation -> review/approval -> trigger sequence.

acceptanceCriteria: A Mission whose frozen source files are unchanged reports no drift.
Modifying a frozen local file marks context stale with the exact source and old/new hashes.
Stale Missions never silently inherit new content; UI/API exposes explicit stale state.
Recompilation produces a new bundle hash, exact spec revision, and new assurance profile receipt; the prior profile cannot apply to the new revision.
The changed revision requires re-review before execution is affected.
Focused tests cover unchanged, changed, deleted, unavailable, profile invalidation, and stale-evidence rejection paths; backend typecheck passes.
userStories.description: Re-hash each frozen source of an approved Mission and compare it to the recorded contentHash. When a source changes, mark the Mission context stale without silently swapping content; expose the exact old/new hash and source state. Bounded recompilation produces a new SourceBundleV1, a new spec revision, and a new assurance profile compilation receipt. The old profile and evidence remain bound to their historical revision but cannot satisfy gates for the new revision. Unknown and unavailable are distinct honest states.
userStories.title: Source-drift detection with revision and assurance invalidation

acceptanceCriteria: The Intent lens renders the frozen source bundle: source count, titles, revisions, hashes, and citations

Drift state renders honestly (no drift / stale / unavailable) with a single dominant action

WCAG: keyboard navigable citation links, accessible hash chip labels, no color-only semantics; 390px no overflow

userStories.description: Extend the Mission Workspace Intent lens (src/panels/MissionWorkspacePanel.tsx, src/components/mission/) to show source provenance: Built from N sources with exact revisions/hashes, included vs excluded sections, citations linking requirements to source passages, conflict resolutions, and drift state.
